The repair journey

From first call to keys in hand.

A general outline. Every repair is different, and we’ll walk you through yours.

Repair order · JCH Auto Works LLCPalmyra, NY
Step 1 · First contact

Tell us what happened

  • Call, stop by, or send photos online.
  • Not drivable? Call and we’ll plan how to get it here.

Tip: wide photos from all four corners help as much as close-ups.

Step 2 · Free

Inspection & estimate

  • We inspect the vehicle and write a free estimate.
  • We explain it line by line.

Shop term: teardown. Removing damaged parts to see the full repair before work begins.

Step 3 · Insurance

Repair plan & approval

  • We work with your adjuster and document the repair.
  • In New York, the choice of repair shop is yours.

Shop term: supplement. An added estimate sent to the insurer when hidden damage is found.

Step 4 · In the shop

Repair & checks

  • Body, structural and paint work by an experienced, I-CAR certified team.
  • You get repair updates along the way.

Any scans or calibrations your vehicle needs are identified up front.

Step 5 · Pickup

Back on the road

  • We walk you through the work that was done.
  • Lifetime workmanship warranty while you own the vehicle.

Parts carry the manufacturer’s warranty.

Insurance & collision guidance

Straight answers to common questions.

What should I do right after a collision?

Get to safety and call 911 if anyone is hurt. Exchange information, photograph the scene and every vehicle, and notify your insurer. In New York, a crash with injury, death, or property damage over $1,000 must be reported to the DMV on form MV-104 within 10 days. Then call us for the next step.

Do I have to use the shop my insurance company suggests?

No. New York law gives you the right to choose where your vehicle is repaired. Your insurer can recommend a shop, but the choice is yours.

Can you help with my insurance claim?

Yes. We work with all major insurance companies. We communicate with your provider and make sure the repair is documented according to their guidelines. Coverage decisions are between you and your insurer, and we keep you informed.

What if more damage is found after the repair starts?

It’s common. Removing damaged parts often reveals damage behind them. It gets documented, sent to your insurer for approval if a claim is involved, and discussed with you before any extra work.
